passage: I'm Sahil from the second floor, and this is what I saw. I was carrying groceries into the lift when little Dolma from the third floor stood behind her mother's leg. Her mother said, "Say namaste to Sahil uncle." Dolma peeked out, said "Ha-llo" to my shoes and hid again. Next morning she said, "My name is Dolma," clearly, then went quiet. Maybe she's shy, or maybe she was just tired. I said, "Thank you for saying hello," and left it there.

qa.q: Where did Sahil first meet Dolma in the passage?
qa.a: At the lift, where he was carrying groceries.

qa.q: Why might Dolma have hidden behind her mother's leg?
qa.a: Most likely shyness with a grown-up she barely knows. Another reading is that she was simply tired.

qa.q: How could Dolma's mother support her learning to greet?
qa.a: Keep prompting kindly and let her greet in her own time, accepting a quiet hello without pressure.

qa.q: How does Sahil seem to feel about Dolma's greeting?
qa.a: Warm and unbothered. He thanked her and left it there, so he seems to treat her small hello as enough. 🙂

grounding: Shows a preschooler learning to greet and give her name with prompting, with shyness respected, seen by a neighbour.

passage: On his first day at nursery, Pranav, five, held his father's hand and said nothing when Vidya Miss said good morning. On the fourth day she crouched and asked, "Can you tell me your name?" Pranav whispered "Pranav" and looked at the floor. On the tenth day he walked in, said, "Good morning, Miss," and when she handed him the crayon box he said, "Thank you!" loudly, then grinned at his father by the door.

qa.q: What did Pranav say when Vidya handed him the crayon box?
qa.a: "Thank you!"

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling on his first day, and what else could explain his silence?
qa.a: Probably shyness in a new place, shown by holding his father's hand and staying silent. He could also have been sleepy or just not ready to speak.

qa.q: What did Vidya do that helped Pranav?
qa.a: She crouched to his level and asked a small question without forcing a reply, giving him time until he was ready.

qa.q: How might Pranav's father have felt on the tenth day?
qa.a: Probably proud and perhaps relieved, since Pranav grinned at him after speaking up.

grounding: Shows a preschooler gradually learning to greet, give a name and say thank you, with shyness respected.

passage: The wedding hall was crowded and loud, and Manoj had only a minute before the photos. He spotted his boss. “Pradeep, say hello to Sharma Sir. Tell him your name.” Pradeep pressed his face into Manoj's side and said nothing. The boss smiled. Manoj felt a flush of embarrassment but didn't push. “He's shy with new people. He'll say hello when he's ready.” Later, at the food counter, Pradeep took a plate from a waiter and whispered, “Thank you.” Manoj squeezed his shoulder.

qa.q: What did Pradeep whisper at the food counter?
qa.a: “Thank you.”

qa.q: What was Pradeep feeling when he pressed his face into Manoj's side?
qa.a: He was shy and overwhelmed by the crowded, loud hall and a stranger asking for his name.

qa.q: Which choice by Manoj worked, and why?
qa.a: He respected Pradeep's shyness instead of pushing, and Pradeep later said thank you on his own.

qa.q: How did the moment feel for Manoj?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed in front of his boss but chose to protect Pradeep's comfort.

grounding: A preschooler goes quiet and hides when prompted to greet a stranger, his father respects it, and later he says thank you.

passage: New neighbours moved into the flat opposite. Tarun's mother knocked with a plate of laddoos, Tarun holding the edge. A tall man opened the door. Tarun's mother whispered, “Say hello and your name.” Tarun took a breath. “Hello. I'm Tarun. I'm five.” The man bent down. “Hello, Tarun. I'm Deepak. Thank you for the laddoos.” Tarun looked at his mother, who nodded, and he added, “You're welcome.” Walking back, he said, “I did it all by myself. Almost.”

qa.q: What did Tarun's mother bring on the plate?
qa.a: Laddoos.

qa.q: What was Tarun feeling when he said, “I did it all by myself. Almost”?
qa.a: He felt proud of greeting Deepak, while honestly noticing that his mother's prompts had helped.

qa.q: What small step helped Tarun greet the new neighbour?
qa.a: His mother's quiet prompt, “Say hello and your name,” and her nod helped him know what to say.

qa.q: How might Deepak feel being greeted by Tarun?
qa.a: He likely feels welcomed and pleased by the friendly introduction from a new neighbour.

grounding: A preschooler learns to say hello, give his name and say you're welcome with adult prompting.

passage:
“Remember what we say at the shop?” Noor Khala asked on the stairs.
“Hello,” said Yusuf.
“And if they ask your name?”
“My name is Yusuf.”
“And when he gives the sweets?”
“Um…”
“Thank…”
“Thank you!”
At the counter, the shopkeeper said, “Hello, young man. What's your name?” Yusuf looked at Khala, swallowed, and said very quietly, “Yusuf.” The shopkeeper handed over the sweets. Yusuf whispered, “Thank you.” Outside, Khala hugged him. “Perfect.” “I forgot hello,” he said. “Next time.”

qa.q: What did the shopkeeper hand over?
qa.a: The sweets.

qa.q: What was Yusuf feeling at the counter when he spoke very quietly?
qa.a: He was nervous and shy with the shopkeeper, though he still wanted to try what he had practised.

qa.q: What helped Yusuf say his name and thank you?
qa.a: Noor Khala practised the words with him on the stairs and prompted him gently.

qa.q: How might Noor Khala see Yusuf forgetting hello?
qa.a: She sees it as normal and is proud of what he managed, which is why she said “Perfect” and hugged him.

grounding: A preschooler practises greeting, giving his name and saying thank you with an adult's prompting.

passage:
Note from Aparna, open-house morning, Nursery B

Mahima arrived with her grandmother, who said, "Say hello to Aparna Ma'am. Tell her your name." Mahima slipped behind her grandmother's sari and peeped out.

I said, "That's all right. Hello, Mahima," and gave a small wave. I didn't ask again.

We looked at the class fish together, from a distance. When I gave her a star sticker at the end, she whispered, "Thank you," and then, very quietly, "I'm Mahima."

She is shy with new places. I'll let her greet in her own time. 🙂

qa.q: What did Mahima slip behind?
qa.a: Her grandmother's sari.

qa.q: What was Mahima feeling when she peeped out from behind her grandmother?
qa.a: She was most likely shy in a new place with a new adult. Her quiet "Thank you" and "I'm Mahima" later suggest she felt safer once nobody pushed her.

qa.q: What choice did Aparna make, and why did it help?
qa.a: Aparna said hello, waved once and did not insist, so Mahima could greet in her own time, which she did at the end.

qa.q: How might Mahima's grandmother feel when Mahima hides?
qa.a: She might feel a little embarrassed or worried that Mahima seems rude, which is why she prompts her to say hello.

grounding: It shows a preschooler prompted to say hello and her name who hides out of shyness, and an adult respecting it until she greets on her own.
